---
id: GM-2
title: "Spike: Git on the device with a Rust core"
type: spike
status: in-progress
priority: urgent
estimate: 4d
remaining: 1d
milestone: M0
depends_on: [GM-1]
---

Prove that a phone can do what the app needs from Git, before anything is built on it. See [[Architecture#git-on-the-device]].

Done when, on a real Android phone and a real iPhone, a test screen can do each step against a private GitHub repository over HTTPS and over SSH:

- [x] Rust crate `native/genbeya_core` with `git2` (vendored libgit2, OpenSSL, libssh2), bound with flutter_rust_bridge
- [x] Shallow single-branch clone of genbeya/genbeya; time and size noted
- [x] Commit a changed file without a staging step
- [x] Fetch, rebase the local commit onto the remote, push
- [x] Commit onto another branch's tree without checking it out (for the content branch)
- [x] `log` for one path, `diff` from a merge base, `merge-tree` style conflict check
- [x] In-memory rebase that leaves the working tree alone until it succeeds
- [x] `core.symlinks=false`, no submodules or LFS; stale lock files after the app is killed
- [x] Note the build steps and what broke (`native/genbeya_core/README.md`); the Rust core works, so it stays (D3 in [[Decisions]])
- [x] On a real Android phone (Pixel 9 Pro XL, 2026-11-21): 120 CA certificates from Android's store; HTTPS clone of genbeya/genbeya at depth 50 in 2.8 s over 5G (2.5 MB received, 7.3 MB on disk); commits in 48–259 ms; Sync without a token fails as it should, with the typed `authFailed` error
- [x] Push with a token on the phone (2026-11-21, a throwaway private repository): clone 2.0 s, commit 59 ms, Sync (fetch, rebase, push) 2.3 s over 5G. A token without write access was refused with HTTP 403, which reached the screen as a generic `Git` error; the core now reports 401 and 403 as `AuthFailed`, so the app can say the token can't write there
- [ ] SSH against a real server, on the phone
- [ ] The same on an iPhone (waits for a Mac)

On this Linux container: 11 flow tests (two clones playing teammates against a bare remote, shallow clones over `git daemon`) and the bridge test from Dart pass; a real depth-1 HTTPS clone of genbeya/genbeya took 1.1 s (1.8 MB received, 8.4 MB on disk). The Android app builds with `libgenbeya_core.so` for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64, about 7 MB each in release (+7.6 MB to an arm64 release APK, mostly OpenSSL). In CI the app also builds for iOS with the Rust core, OpenSSL and libssh2 (unsigned; it needed `-lz -liconv` in the plugin's pod, since libgit2 uses the system's zlib and iconv on Apple platforms). Not run yet: a real phone, SSH against a real server, HTTPS push with a token.

First run on a Pixel 9 Pro XL (2026-11-21): the clone failed, and the screen showed `head()`'s "failed to resolve path" instead of the clone's own error, because flutter_rust_bridge drops what a streaming function returns. Clone and fetch now end their stream with `Done` or `Failed` carrying the typed error (`runTransfer` in `lib/access/native/transfers.dart`). The likely cause of the failure itself: OpenSSL was pointed at Android's CA folder, whose files are named by OpenSSL's old hash and which, since Android 14, lives in the Conscrypt module; the app now writes the system's certificates into one PEM file (`lib/access/native/ca_bundle.dart`). The first version of that hung the app at the splash screen: it ran before `runApp`, and an exception from listing the certificate folder ended `main`. Now the certificates come from Android's own store (`AndroidCAStore`, through a channel in `MainActivity.kt`), with the folders as fallback; the setup runs after the app is up, never throws, and the Git core screen shows what it found. On the phone that showed the real cause: OpenSSL failed to load the bundle ("BIO lib"), because the vendored OpenSSL is built with `no-stdio` on Android and can't open files at all. The certificates now go to the core in memory, DER-encoded (`add_ca_certificates`, libgit2's `GIT_OPT_ADD_SSL_X509_CERT`), tested with the machine's CA bundle. To try again on the phone.

Proven on Linux with OpenSSL's own locations emptied: a real HTTPS clone trusting only the 121 certificates added from memory succeeds (`tests/certificates.rs`, ignored test).

Found on the way, in libgit2 1.9.7: when a TLS certificate check fails behind an HTTP proxy, `http_client_connect` frees the proxy stream before closing the TLS stream that runs over it, and the TLS shutdown then writes into the freed stream (`transports/httpclient.c`, `on_error`). Here it hung for good; it could crash. Phones connect directly unless a proxy is set, and there a bad certificate fails cleanly (226 ms on the Pixel). To do: report it to libgit2; if we keep libgit2, patch the order (close the server stream before the proxy). The core now sets network timeouts (15 s to connect, 60 s per read or write), which libgit2 has none of by default.

Confirm the decided editor, CodeMirror 6 in the kit for pages and code, against a native one on real phones (D4 in [[Decisions]]). Comments use a native text field. See [[Architecture#the-web-kit]].

- [x] CodeMirror 6 in the kit, with Genbeya's Markdown language and `[[` completion
- [x] re_editor (or another maintained native editor) with Markdown highlighting
- [x] Try each on a 2,000-line Markdown file: typing, autocorrect, the system keyboard's suggestions, selection handles, undo, scrolling, a toolbar above the keyboard
- [x] Confirm CodeMirror 6 on both phones; only if it fails, the code editor goes native, and record it in [[Architecture]] (confirmed on Android; the iPhone waits for a Mac, with the rest of the trial build)

In Chromium with Pixel 7 and iPhone 15 emulation: tap, type, complete by tapping, select and undo work; toolbar commands, drafts and save with the base hash too. Autocorrect, input methods, selection handles and the keyboard toolbar can only be judged on real phones.

Spike screens (2026-11-21): **Editor (kit)** opens CodeMirror 6 in the kit full screen with Genbeya's completions, a native toolbar above the keyboard and a status line (selection, drafts, save); **Editor (native)** opens re_editor 0.10 on the same text with the same toolbar, without completions. Both switch to a 2,000-line page. The first build had no editor screen at all (the tile led nowhere); this one is to try on the Pixel.

On the Pixel: the kit's editor opens and highlights Markdown, but its toolbar sat under Android's navigation bar; re_editor's plain text was nearly invisible (its default text colour on the app's dark background). Both fixed: the toolbar stays in the safe area, and re_editor takes the app's colours.

Second try on the Pixel: both editors open, are readable and keep the toolbar above the keyboard. The red underlines in the kit's editor come from the keyboard's spell checker (set to German, checking English text); whether code files should turn spell checking off is for the editor work. Left: which one feels better to type in, which decides D4.

**Outcome (2026-11-21):** the kit's editor wins, and D4 stands. On the Pixel it runs the 2,000-line page without a hitch, and it has what the native editor would need written again: the `[[`, `@` and `//` completions. Spell checking in code files is left for the code editor ([[GM-17]]).

The Dart engines needed to show a repository, each checked by conformance cases. See [[Architecture#engines]].

- [x] Contracts mirroring `model.ts`: `Settings`, `WikiNode`, `FileNode`, `Task`, `Person`, field definitions
- [x] Settings: every key, defaults and validation, `unused` and the automatic parts (ported with [[GM-5]], every key of `Settings` in `model.ts`)
- [x] Wiki tree and titles from file names (`wiki_engine.dart`, `file_tree.dart`; sorted by `collation.dart`, ICU's order without ICU)
- [x] Tasks: parsing, epics, comments section, custom field kinds (effort, tasks, date, choice); the time log split is only used by a task's activity, so it moved to [[GM-9]] with `changesBetween`
- [x] People and handles, and "me" (`people_engine.dart`, `people.dart`)
- [x] References: resolving `[[…]]` to tasks, pages and files happens in the kit, with Genbeya's own code, from the context the host sends; the native side needs it first for search and links, so the Dart port moved to [[GM-10]]
- [x] `.genbeya-content` and the content branch layout (read only): `content_layout.dart`, `RepositoryModel.locate`
- [x] Event-driven repository model instead of polled snapshots, with a parse cache by blob ID ([[Call chains#the-repository-model]]): the model and its in-memory cache; the app's own writes updating it directly come with the writes ([[GM-11]]), keeping the cache across starts with the first screens that need fast cold starts ([[GM-9]])
- [x] On resume, `status` catches changes made outside the app: the model reads Git's objects, not the working tree, so only uncommitted writes of the app itself can differ, which the write journal handles ([[GM-11]])

Wiki tree (2026-11-22): `WikiEngine` and `buildFileTree` are ported; 20 cases build the file and wiki trees of Genbeya, of this repository and of an edge list (case, accents, numbers, punctuation, folders with and without pages, `.MD`, other scripts, emoji; wiki roots `docs`, a subfolder, `` and `.`) and match Genbeya's output. The sorting needed ICU's collation in Dart: a table generated from Node's ICU, checked by 42 `collate` cases; on 1,511 strings all 2.3 million pairs compare as ICU compares them. Desktop sorts in the user's locale, so a Swedish or Danish desktop may order some titles differently; the phone follows ICU's root order, which English, German and most locales share.

People (2026-11-22): `PeopleEngine.merge` and `me`, and the handle and mention rules, are ported. Five cases merge people from the settings, made-up commit authors (no real emails in the fixtures), assignees and comment authors: aliases, plus addresses and GitHub's noreply addresses, generic mailboxes, handle collisions (`emile-2`), accents, other scripts and emoji (falling back to `person`), the 39-character cap, and 120 random authors; all match Genbeya. Sorting people needed `localeCompare` at full strength and `normalize("NFD")`, both from the generated table.

Repository model (2026-11-22): the core reads files from Git's objects (`resolve_commit`, `list_files` with blob IDs, `read_blobs` in one call, `read_file_at`, `changed_paths`, `config_value`; a flow test). `RepositoryModel` locates each area (checkout or content branch, by `.genbeya-content`, read as `git config` reads it: 24 conformance cases run real `git config --list`), then reads settings, the wiki tree, tasks (problems listed by file) and the people the settings, assignees and comments name, with parses cached by blob. Tested with a fake over every layout and over a real clone through the bridge. People also count the authors of HEAD's newest 5,000 commits as `.mailmap` names them (`commit_authors` in the core, read again only when HEAD moves), and `me` is who Git signs commits as in the clone (`user.name`, `user.email`, which the app sets per repository in [[GM-6]]). Not yet: keeping the cache across app starts.

id: GM-11
title: Commit, sync and the Genbeya merge
type: feature
status: backlog
priority: urgent
estimate: 5d
remaining: 5d
milestone: M2
depends_on: [GM-2, GM-7]
---

How mobile edits reach everyone, without ever losing one. See [[Architecture#where-edits-go]] and [[Experience#sync-and-changes]].

- [ ] Every save is a commit named after the change and the task, with the repository's identity
- [ ] Where commits go: the content branch for its areas, else asked on the first edit with the checked-out branch offered; a refused push offers to move the unpushed commits to `mobile/<handle>` (D5)
- [ ] Sync: fetch, rebase, push, one at a time per repository; pull to refresh; optional automatic sync
- [ ] Genbeya merge for task and pull request files: frontmatter per key, signed lines from both sides; conformance cases for it
- [ ] Rescue branch `mobile/rescue/<handle>-<date>` when it still conflicts: pushed, a banner of what differs until its commits are upstream, then an offer to delete it (D6)
- [ ] **Changes**: unsynced commits, undo the last ones before they are pushed
- [ ] Write journal: a write and its commit as one unit, recovered on the next start
- [ ] Never force; retry a rejected push from fetch, up to 3 times; rebase in memory
- [ ] Renumber a local, unpushed task whose ID a teammate took meanwhile, and the references to it in local commits
- [ ] Renumbering a task also moves its `.images/<ID>/` folder and rewrites its image references ([[Attached images]])
